I'm working in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-agent-moddesc (a checkout of the Nxeon platform repo). I need to add a new weekly scheduled job that re-runs several mod-catalog importer scripts (scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts, scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts, scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts, and scripts/verify-gamemods.ts) on a schedule, since nothing currently does.

Please research and report back (do NOT make any edits, this is read-only research):

1. How does this codebase currently run PERIODIC/RECURRING background jobs? Look specifically at:
   - worker/index.ts and any other files in worker/ — is there a cron-style scheduler, an interval loop, or anything that runs "every N hours/days"? Grep for terms like "cron", "setInterval", "schedule", "every", "daily", "weekly", "systemd timer" references in comments.
   - Are there existing systemd timer unit files or references to them anywhere in the repo (e.g. under a `systemd/` or `deploy/` or `ops/` directory, or referenced in scripts/*.sh, or CLAUDE.md, or docs/DOCUMENTATION.md)?
   - Search for any existing "recurring task"/"scheduled task" pattern already in use for OTHER periodic maintenance (e.g. renewals, email digests, backups, cache warming, blog SEO refresh, anything that says "runs weekly" or "runs daily" or "runs every X hours" in a comment).
   - Check package.json's "scripts" section for any npm script names suggestive of periodic jobs.

2. Once you find the established pattern (I strongly suspect it's either (a) a systemd timer unit + a script entrypoint, or (b) a setInterval-style loop inside worker/index.ts, or (c) something else entirely), report:
   - The exact file(s) that implement an existing example of it (give me full paths and the relevant line ranges).
   - The exact shape/convention I should copy (e.g. is there a systemd .timer + .service file pair checked into the repo under a specific directory? What does the .service ExecStart look like — does it call `npx tsx scripts/whatever.ts` directly, or a wrapper shell script? Is there a lockfile/concurrency guard pattern? How are logs handled — journald, a log file?).
   - Whether such jobs are installed/enabled via a setup script (e.g. `scripts/install-timers.sh` or similar) that I'd also need to update, or whether they're installed manually via `systemctl enable` outside the repo (in which case the repo would just document it).

Report back concisely: the exact pattern to follow, the exact files involved, and any gotchas (e.g. "must run as root because X", "must set NXEON_DB_TARGET", "logs go to journalctl -u nxeon-X"). Keep the report under 400 words plus code citations.

===NIGHTLY TIMER===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon nightly signal scan (~03:30)

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:30:00
# Catch up on the most recent missed run if the host was off at 03:30.
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
===NIGHTLY SERVICE===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon nightly signal scanner (writes proposals to the Improvements board)
Documentation=https://nxeon.local/docs
After=network-online.target postgresql.service
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=nxeon
Group=nxeon
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon
# Loads DATABASE_URL and the rest of the app environment.
EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx tsx scripts/nightly-scan.ts
# Reading the service journals needs the systemd-journal group. Harmless if the
# nxeon user is not a member — the journalctl collector fails soft (try/catch).
SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal
TimeoutStartSec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

===BACKUP VMS TIMER===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon daily whole-system backup (host config + every guest, ~04:30)
# ROOT CAUSE THIS FILE FIXES — whole-system backups had NEVER run.
#
# This timer previously read `OnCalendar=Sun *-*-* 04:30:00`. It was enabled at
# 2026-07-23 11:36:20 UTC, a THURSDAY, so its first eligible fire was Sunday
# 2026-07-26 04:30 — three days later. `Persistent=true` did not back-fill,
# because Persistent= only replays an elapse that was *missed while the timer was
# inactive*, and that is computed from
# /var/lib/systemd/timers/stamp-nxeon-backup-vms.timer, which did not exist until
# the first genuine trigger wrote it. A never-triggered timer has no missed
# elapse to replay. Nothing was misconfigured; the weekly schedule itself
# guaranteed a multi-day window in which a live host with real customer VMs held
# zero whole-VM backups, and `OnFailure=nxeon-alert@` could not report it because
# a unit that never runs never fails.
#
# Daily is the owner's stated cadence ("back up the entire system once every day,
# store the latest 3") and it also bounds this failure class: the worst case for a
# freshly installed daily timer is under 24 hours instead of a week.
#
# After enabling this timer, run the unit once by hand — `systemctl start
# nxeon-backup-vms.service` — rather than waiting for the window. /admin/backups
# flags any timer whose LastTriggerUSec is empty precisely so this is visible.

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:30:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=600

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
===BACKUP VMS SERVICE===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon whole-system backup (/etc/pve + every guest via vzdump)
Wants=pve-cluster.service
After=pve-cluster.service pvedaemon.service
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-vms.sh
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=best-effort
IOSchedulingPriority=7
# Type=oneshot defaults to TimeoutStartUSec=infinity. That is a second silent-stall
# mode on top of the never-fired timer: if vzdump wedges (network-dark storage,
# half-open QMP), the unit sits in "activating" forever, systemd refuses to start
# an already-active oneshot so every subsequent daily trigger is skipped, and
# OnFailure= never fires because nothing has failed. One hung run would mean no
# backups again, indefinitely, showing no error. 6h is ~35x the observed 04:31 run
# (3m29s CPU / ~5min wall for 6 guests) and comfortable for 16 including templates.
TimeoutStartSec=6h
===VERIFY RESTORE TIMER===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon daily backup restore verification (~05:30)
# SAME ROOT CAUSE AS nxeon-backup-vms.timer, AND STILL LIVE WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN.
#
# This timer read `OnCalendar=Mon 05:30` and was enabled 2026-07-24 04:10:54 UTC,
# a FRIDAY — so its first eligible fire was Monday 2026-07-27 and
# `systemctl show nxeon-verify-restore.timer -p LastTriggerUSec` was EMPTY:
# restore verification had never once run on a schedule. The 2026-07-24 timestamp
# that makes it look like it ran is (a) the mtime of
# /var/lib/systemd/timers/stamp-nxeon-verify-restore.timer, written when the timer
# was first started, and (b) a one-off manual `systemctl start
# nxeon-verify-restore.service` by whoever installed it. Neither is a timer run.
#
# Daily, so it verifies the daily backup it is supposed to be verifying, and so a
# mid-week install cannot leave it dormant for the better part of a week.
# Scheduled after nxeon-backup-vms (04:30) and nxeon-backup-offsite (04:20) so it
# checks the freshest set.

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 05:30:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
===VERIFY RESTORE SERVICE===
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon backup restore verification (restores newest dump into a scratch DB)
Wants=postgresql.service
After=postgresql.service
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/verify-restore.sh
Nice=10
# See nxeon-backup-vms.service: Type=oneshot defaults to an infinite start timeout,
# so a hung psql restore would park the unit in "activating" forever and silently
# suppress every future trigger without ever reporting a failure.
TimeoutStartSec=1h

# Nxeon nightly scanner

Server-side, laptop-independent scan that runs on the Proxmox host and writes
deduped proposals into the `Improvement` table (admin Improvements board). It
gathers read-only signals — recurring server-log errors, failed jobs, failed
emails, stuck jobs, new feedback, bug-flagged tickets, and open abuse alerts —
and never reproposes a finding that is already active on the board.

## Install + enable the timer

```bash
# Copy the units into place
sudo cp /opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo cp /opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.timer   /etc/systemd/system/

# Reload systemd and enable the daily timer (fires ~03:30, catches up if missed)
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nxeon-nightly-scan.timer
```

## Verify / operate

```bash
# See when it will next run
systemctl list-timers nxeon-nightly-scan.timer

# Run it once right now (writes real proposals)
sudo systemctl start nxeon-nightly-scan.service

# Inspect the last run's output
journalctl -u nxeon-nightly-scan.service --no-pager -n 20
```

The service runs as `User=nxeon` with `EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env`. It is a
`oneshot` unit driven entirely by the timer — enabling the timer is all that is
needed. Reading the service journals uses the `systemd-journal` supplementary
group; if the `nxeon` user is not in that group the log-error collector simply
returns nothing (the rest of the scan still runs).

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — whole-system backup (host config + every guest), run DAILY, keep 3.
#
# Step 1: scripts/backup-pve-config.sh  — /etc/pve and friends (see that file).
# Step 2: vzdump of every QEMU guest with VMID in [100, 9000), plus the OS
#         templates when NXEON_VM_BACKUP_INCLUDE_TEMPLATES=1 (the default).
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHERE THESE ARCHIVES GO, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE `backup` STORAGE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This script used to run `vzdump --storage backup`, which writes into
# /tank/backup/dump — the same Proxmox storage a customer's own on-demand backups
# land in. lib/proxmox.ts `pruneBackups` then selected deletion victims with
# nothing but `b.vmid === vmid`, so a customer clicking "Create backup" pruned
# *every* archive for their VMID down to CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP (2) — including the
# platform's host-level disaster-recovery copy of that same VM. On 2026-07-26 the
# 04:31 run left vmid 102 holding the customer's manual archive plus a 10 GB
# platform archive; one more customer click would have destroyed the platform's
# only copy. Repeat across the fleet and the entire bare-metal recovery set is
# gone, deleted by customers, with no error anywhere.
#
# So platform archives now go to NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR (/tank/backup/platform)
# via `vzdump --dumpdir`. That directory is NOT the `dump/` subdirectory of any
# configured PVE storage, and Proxmox only indexes `<storage-path>/dump`. The
# archives therefore have no `volid`: they cannot appear in the
# /storage/backup/content listing that customer retention iterates, and no volid
# string exists that `DELETE /storage/backup/content/<volid>` could resolve to
# them. Customer retention cannot reach them because it cannot name them.
#
# vzdump's own `--prune-backups` still works in dumpdir mode (PVE::VZDump
# get_backup_file_list + prune_mark_backup_group), scoped to files matching
# `vzdump-<type>-<vmid>-*` inside that one directory — so platform retention only
# ever prunes platform archives.
#
# FALLBACK MODE: setting NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE=<sid> restores the old
# shared-storage behaviour for operators who want these visible in the Proxmox UI.
# In that mode every archive is stamped with `--notes-template` carrying the
# platform marker and its volid is appended to PROTECTED-VOLIDS, both of which
# lib/proxmox.ts honours — so the invariant holds there too, just by convention
# rather than by construction. Dumpdir mode is the default for that reason.

All three importers default to a dry run and require an explicit `--apply` flag; `verify-gamemods.ts` has no such flag (it always writes) and takes no `NXEON_DB_TARGET` guard. I have everything needed.

## Established pattern: systemd `.timer` + `.service` pair under `deploy/`, entrypoint script(s) under `scripts/`

**Reference example (copy this shape):** `deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.timer` + `deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.service` + `scripts/nightly-scan.ts`, documented in `deploy/NIGHTLY-SCAN-README.md`. Also `deploy/nxeon-backup-vms.timer/.service` and `deploy/nxeon-verify-restore.timer/.service` (paired with `scripts/backup-vms.sh` / `scripts/verify-restore.sh`) show the same convention for shell-script entrypoints.

- **Timer** (`deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.timer`): `[Timer] OnCalendar=...`, `Persistent=true` (catch up on missed runs), `RandomizedDelaySec=...`; `[Install] WantedBy=timers.target`. For weekly, use e.g. `OnCalendar=Mon *-*-* 03:30:00`.
- **Service** (`deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.service`, lines 1-19): `Type=oneshot`, `User=nxeon`/`Group=nxeon`, `WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon`, `EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env`, `ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx tsx scripts/whatever.ts` (direct tsx invocation, no wrapper shell script needed for TS entrypoints — shell wrappers like `backup-vms.sh` are only used when the job itself is a bash script), `TimeoutStartSec=<generous, oneshot default is infinite>`, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`.
- **Concurrency guard**: no flock/lockfile anywhere in the repo. The guard is `Type=oneshot` itself — systemd refuses to start an already-active oneshot unit, so overlapping runs are structurally prevented as long as `TimeoutStartSec` is set (the backup-vms service comment explains why an unset timeout is dangerous: a hung run blocks all future triggers silently).
- **Logs**: journald only — `journalctl -u nxeon-<name>.service --no-pager -n 20`. No log files.
- **Install**: manual, documented in a README (`deploy/NIGHTLY-SCAN-README.md`), NOT an install script — `sudo cp deploy/*.timer deploy/*.service /etc/systemd/system/ && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --now nxeon-<name>.timer`. (`scripts/onboard-node.sh` does auto-install `nxeon-backup-vms.timer`, but that's for fresh host bootstrap, not a pattern you need to touch for this job — write a companion `deploy/*-README.md` instead, matching nightly-scan's.)

## Gotcha (critical): `NXEON_DB_TARGET`

Three of your four scripts — `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts:105-106`, `import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`, `import-thunderstore-catalog.ts` — call `assertDbTarget(...)` from `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` at module load and **exit immediately unless `NXEON_DB_TARGET` is set and matches the database name in `DATABASE_URL`**. I checked `/opt/nxeon/.env`: `NXEON_DB_TARGET` is **not currently set there**, and `DATABASE_URL`'s db name is `nxeon`. No existing timer service sets this var (nightly-scan/backup services don't need it). You must add `Environment=NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon` to the new `.service` unit (or add the line to `/opt/nxeon/.env`) or the weekly job will fail every run with a refusal. `verify-gamemods.ts` has no such guard — it always writes.

All three importers also default to dry-run; ExecStart needs `--apply` explicitly, e.g. `ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx tsx scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts --apply`. `import-modrinth-catalog.ts`'s own header comment (lines 4-6) already says "run verify-gamemods.ts afterward on a schedule" — confirming no schedule exists yet. Chain all four in one `ExecStart` (e.g. `sh -c '... && ... && ... && ...'`) or four separate `ExecStartPre`/sequential services, since each is a separate `npx tsx` invocation and a single oneshot only runs one `ExecStart` command list sequentially if written as `&&`.
